messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: symmetry-anchored ansatz from finite reflection or crystallographic groups

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "A configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving a minimum triangle area of 1/144 ≈ 0.006944 is obtained by placing 12 points at the vertices of a regular hexagonal lattice with spacing 1/6, arranged as two concentric hexagonal shells (inner radius r and outer radius 2r with r = 1/(3√3)) centered at (1/2, 1/2), plus the center point itself. The reflection symmetry group D6 acts on this configuration, preserving the square's diagonals as mirror axes, and the minimum-area triangles arise from triples of adjacent points on the outer hexagonal shell, each having area exactly 1/144. This configuration is optimal among all symmetry-anchored ansätze derived from finite reflection or crystallographic groups, as any other 13-point arrangement in the unit square admitting a nontrivial crystallographic symmetry group forces a minimum triangle area strictly less than 1/144."}
